Luther’s understanding of the gospel is the key for his theology, and the gospel is the power of God unto salvation (Romans 1:16). This gospel is the good news that God’s grace has been given to us through the work of Christ on the cross.
Luther is a theologian of the cross.

Luther’s theology of the cross, as the heart of his theology, is not only the foundation for his doctrine of justification by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone, but it also serves as the foundation for his entire theological system and his understanding of Christian living.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Reformation is not over, nor is it finished.
Luther’s theology of the cross, his understanding of the law and gospel, his theology of justification, and his doctrine of the sacraments are still very much in play in our own day.
Luther’s theology is not only a theological and ecclesial watershed, but it is also a theological and ecclesiastical watershed that is still being worked out.
